newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea's Feb trade deficit widens to $2.1 bln. [CORRECTED 06:31 GMT]
newsitem.headline: South Korea's Feb trade deficit widens to $2.1 bln. [CORRECTED 06:31 GMT]

text.p: South Korea's customs-cleared trade deficit widened to $2.1 billion in February from a $1.6 billion shortfall a year earlier, provisional figures released by the trade ministry showed on Monday.
(Corrects years in column heads for the table.)
NOTE: in millions of dollars, January figures revised.
The ministry said in a statment FOB exports fell 4.9 percent in February on the year, and CIF imports increased 0.1 percent.
Semiconductor exports in the month fell 41 percent as a result of falling prices.
"Unit price for the 16-megbit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips fell 78 percent in February from a year earlier," the statement said.
However, exports improved from January, which had been hit by almost a month of wildcat strikes. The January deficit was revised downward to $3.39 billion from $3.48 billion, the ministry said.
The ministry hopes this year's deficit would shrink to $14 billion from $20.62 billion.
"The trade deficit for the first quarter will be less than $8 billion. That's a good news because we earlier forecast a deficit well over $8 billion," said a trade ministry official said.
The ministry's statement said improvement in exports was pronounced in the sectors of auto parts and oil products.
Exports of auto parts during the first 20 days of February rose 79.5 percent, oil products jumped 103 percent and computers 22.5 percent.
The ministry said exports of electronic parts and vehicles in February dropped 28.8 percent and 37.1 percent, respectively.
Overall, exports of heavy industrial goods fell 11 percent in the month from a year ago, while those of light industrial products declined 10.6 percent.
Shipments to major industrial nations continued to weaken, with exports to the United States and European Union falling 25.4 percent and 29.1 percent each.
The value of crude oil imports rose 101.7 percent due to rising international prices, while those of machinery fell 14.2 percent, reflecting sluggish capital investment, the ministry said.
